writeup.1: Look at the bottom of a PAYNTR collab and you will find the partner’s name printed across the outsole. Not a logo on the tongue, not a hangtag. The tread. Turn over the Students shoe and STUDENTS reads through translucent rubber; the Forresters shoe says FORRESTERS across the same panel. It is a small decision and most of why these sell out, because the branding stays invisible until somebody is standing behind you on a tee box.
writeup.2: PAYNTR has now done twenty-five collaborations with eleven brands, and thirteen of them landed in the last seventy-two days. The previous twelve run across the nineteen months before that, so the pace has roughly quadrupled this summer, and most of what came out of it has already sold through.
writeup.3: The brand comes from cricket. David Paynter played professionally, is the great-grandson of the England Ashes batsman Eddie Paynter, and started the label in 2017 because cricket footwear was bad. Golf came later, run out of Portland, Oregon with Mike Forsey and Michael Glancy Jr., who both had long careers in performance footwear before this. That background is why the shoes are competent and why the graphics live under them rather than on them.
writeup.4: The partners run from Students and Sugarloaf Social Club through Jones, Khalhon, Bad Birdie, Vessel, Ghost, Forresters, Matchstick and Del Campo, at prices from an eighteen dollar sock to a two hundred and fifty dollar shoe. PAYNTR’s own house line closes it out, and it is plainer than anything the brand makes with somebody else.
